population.note: FICTIONAL estimates. 11.5% of US adults are on an incretin, about 30M of roughly 262M adults. 18% have ever used one. Adoption is nearly flat. Falling prices and pills that work as well as the jab brought in new starters, but almost as many current users quit as the employer retreat continued and the novelty wore off. Cycling arithmetic: 18% ever − 11.5% current = 6.5% of adults who used and are off now. About 35% of current users are restarters, which matches the parent's one-third one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year: 0.35 × 11.5 ≈ 4.0% of adults. About 1.4% of adults are off after at least one restart. (4.0 + 1.4) / 18 ≈ 30% of ever-users have cycled. Age-weighted check, using shares of adults 18–29 20%, 30–49 33%, 50–64 24%, 65+ 23%: 1.0 + 3.3 + 4.8 + 2.4 ≈ 11.5. Use at 65+ rose from 9% to 10.5% through the Medicare Bridge. Use at 50–64 fell from 22% to 20% because that group depends on employer plans. Income thirds average to the national figure: (15 + 12 + 7.5) / 3 = 11.5. The bottom third relies on Medicaid in the states that adopted it and on $149 pills. Payer mix of about 30M users: commercial ~12M, Medicare ~6.8M (diabetes and Bridge obesity), Medicaid ~2.8M, cash ~8.4M. Pediatric: about 0.4% of under-18s. This is concentrated at ages 12–17, where roughly 4% of adolescents with obesity are on a drug. Under-12 use stays specialist-led and still skews affluent. Never-users who would qualify by BMI are about 25% of adults, and most of them cite cost, side effects or the new 'unmedicated' stigma.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge was extended on unchanged terms through Dec 2029 (CMMI demonstration). Medicare pays about $245/month and beneficiaries pay about $50. Of about 6.8M newly eligible beneficiaries (~10% of enrollees), about 1.6M use obesity coverage: 1.6M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.7B/yr gross federal. That is consistent with CBO's ≥$35B over 2026–2034 (~$4B/yr). Fourteen states' Medicaid programmes cover obesity at the same $245 rate, about 0.9M users: 0.9M × $245 × 12 ≈ $2.6B/yr combined federal and state. Diabetes coverage is unchanged in both programmes.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 50+ generic semaglutide brands at about $8–48/month. Canada's generics are about CAD 70–110/month. Brazil and Mexico have generics on the market. Generic injectable and oral semaglutide is available in about 160 countries. Lilly's tirzepatide is still branded everywhere.
access.note: Managed decline through negotiated channels, with no structural change in who pays. Cash channels (TrumpRx, LillyDirect, NovoCare): injectables went from $245–349 (2026) to $199–299. Orals start at $149 and top doses cost $199. Retatrutide (approved Apr 2028) launched at a flat $299 cash. List prices still exist, but under 2% of fills pay them. Employer coverage drifted from 60% to 56%, with no reversal by early droppers such as Starbucks. Prior authorisation and BMI ≥30 (or ≥27 with comorbidity) thresholds are standard. The 503B bulks exclusion was finalised in late 2026, so compounded product is now a marginal illicit trade. Personal importation of Canadian and Indian generic semaglutide is technically unlawful, tolerated at small scale, and estimated at under 3% of US use. Route: weekly injectables are still about 55% of US users by volume, but orals are about 60% of new starts since the 50 mg oral semaglutide reached parity.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg and 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
GLP-1/amylin combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Feb 2027)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Apr 2028)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder with comorbid obesity or type 2 diabetes — guideline-endorsed (ASAM conditional recommendation, Jun 2027; VA formulary); FDA sNDA for semaglutide filed Jun 2028, under review
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol use disorder without obesity — off-label, widely prescribed by addiction clinics since the ASAM guideline
low-dose 'calm/focus' and craving-reduction use marketed by telehealth firms to adults at or near label thresholds
microdosing for 'metabolic health' among non-obese affluent users
nicotine and gambling craving reduction — observational, phase 2 trials ongoing
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: Oral parity is met by an existing product in a new form, as the envelope allows. Novo's oral semaglutide 50 mg was filed as an sNDA in Jan 2027 and approved in Oct 2027 after a 68-week head-to-head trial. It achieved about 16% mean weight loss and was non-inferior to weekly Wegovy 2.4 mg. Separately, Lilly's maintenance data show people who switch from tirzepatide to Foundayo keep most of their loss. No pill yet matches tirzepatide's ~21% or retatrutide's 28%. Retatrutide's BLA was filed in Mar 2027 and approved in Apr 2028 under a priority voucher. Its label carries dysesthesia, and about 11% discontinue for adverse events. CagriSema was approved in Feb 2027 on placebo-controlled data, but uptake is modest after it failed against tirzepatide. Survodutide was filed in Sep 2027, with a decision due in 2028–29. Amycretin is still in phase 3 with no filing. MariTide (monthly) and bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts are not on the US market. The global incretin market is about $105B in 2028. Growth comes from volume while US net price per script falls.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and leading cause of discontinuation. It is slightly lower with slow-titration oral regimens.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; higher absolute rates with retatrutide.
Low absolute risk. Five-year-plus outcome data still show no confirmed causal link.
About 25–30% of weight lost is lean mass. Musculoskeletal and bone-density signals are accumulating in users over 65 as Medicare Bridge use expands.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change. Guidelines recommend resistance training and protein targets, and the muscle-adjunct drugs are still in trials.
EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; still no US class label.
Warning stays removed from Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound labels.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The FDA-required Foundayo postmarketing study used the validated SHAPS anhedonia scale. Pooled with Sentinel claims data, it found clinically meaningful reward blunting in about 4% of patients on maintenance doses vs about 1.5% on placebo. Risk is dose-related and roughly doubled in people with prior depression. Most cases resolve within 4–8 weeks of dose reduction. That gives about 1.2M US adults on-drug affected at any time, attributable excess ~0.75M.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling change, Sep 2027: 'Anhedonia/emotional blunting' added to Adverse Reactions with the prevalence estimate and a dose-reduction recommendation. No boxed warning. No restriction on promotional framing of 'reduced food noise'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Real-world data have converged on about half of lost weight regained within a year (between the trial figure and 2026 claims figures). Switching from injectable to oral reduces regain.
Further observational signals, especially B12, iron and vitamin D in long-term users and adolescents.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; professional societies advise baseline labs.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: There are now about six years of rigorous follow-up. About 30% of ever-users have cycled, and no cycling-specific outcome data exist.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements attached to the retatrutide and CagriSema approvals.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New reports have declined since the 503B exclusion was finalised. There are sporadic counterfeit-pen and imported-generic dosing incidents.
Reported in phase 3 at single-digit percentages, mostly mild and transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Rebound drinking after discontinuation in AUD patients
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Case series from addiction clinics. No controlled data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; mentioned in the ASAM guideline as a monitoring point.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume pressure persists in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks, though adoption is plateauing. Protein and 'GLP-1-friendly' portions are now standard rather than a niche. A small counter-segment of full-fat, 'abundant' premium foods sells to young affluent urban buyers as part of the appetite aesthetic. Analysts are trimming the high end of the $30–55B 2030 revenue-loss estimates because adoption has flattened near 11–12%.

alcohol.state: Since the ASAM guideline in mid-2027, addiction clinics and primary care have been offering semaglutide to heavy drinkers. Treated heavy drinkers are still a small share of the population, but the top decile of drinkers produces about 60% of volume. US spirits volume is down about 3–4% over the window, with brown spirits and on-premise late-night hit hardest. No-alcohol and low-ABV ranges are growing but do not replace the lost margin.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat. Smaller plates and premium 'occasion' ordering are normal. In New York, LA and Austin, tasting menus and family-style 'feast' formats market themselves to an 'unmedicated' crowd, a small but visible inversion.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists continue to shrink through store closures. Mainstream brands have absorbed the re-sizing wave. Athletic and 'muscle-cut' tailoring (broader shoulders, fitted thighs) is the growth line.

fitness.state: The muscle ideal and lean-mass guidance are both driving strength-training growth. Premium gyms sell body-composition scans and 'unmedicated strength' classes, while GLP-1 companion programmes keep serving users on the drug.

insurance.state: No structural shift. Employer coverage drifted from 60% to 56%. Pharmacy trend moderated to about 8% as net prices fell. Prior authorisation and BMI thresholds are standard. Some covering employers steer members to $149–199 orals as first line.

pharma.state: The Novo–Lilly duopoly holds. Lilly leads on efficacy with retatrutide and tirzepatide, while Novo has regained share in orals with the 50 mg pill. Revenue grows on volume and ex-US markets while the US price per script falls about 20–30%. A large GLP-1R pipeline awaits the 2031–32 exclusivity cliff.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among college-educated urban 25–40-year-olds, a merely thin body now reads as 'on it' and therefore unremarkable or slightly suspect. Visible muscle, a big appetite and 'unmedicated' energy now read as scarce. Outside those circles, especially in the suburban Midwest and South, weight loss is still mostly welcomed and the drug is just a prescription.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Thinness has become cheap: a $149 pill. The scarce signals are expensive in time and money: trainers, protein, body-composition scans, and visibly eating whatever you like. The bottom income third still uses the drug least (7.5%). For them the drug is aspirational, while affluent young people distance themselves from it. Many muscular 'unmedicated' influencers have been exposed as on low doses.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller portions remain normal in GLP-1 households. In Brooklyn and Silver Lake, ordering a full plate and finishing it has become a social display, and 'feast' dinners are a dating and status ritual. 'Food noise' is still common language, and having it is half-boasted as proof of being unmedicated.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps added optional lifestyle tags, and 'unmedicated' and 'hungry' trend among users under 35. The anhedonia label gives couples a vocabulary. 'Is it you or the dose?' is a recognised line in couples therapy. Reported libido changes remain anecdotal outside the 4% blunting figure.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has split in meaning. In clinics it is a treatable signal, now explicitly including the craving for drink. In culture, among the young and affluent, it is a mark of vitality and authenticity. The same impulse is sold as a symptom to be quieted and flaunted as a trait.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Labelled since Sep 2027: about 4% clinically meaningful blunting vs 1.5% placebo, dose-related, mostly reversible. Milder flattening below the clinical threshold is common in self-report, unmeasured, and is what is being sold.
interior_life.framing: It is a labelled adverse effect at the clinical end, and a feature, 'quiet', at the subclinical end. Manufacturers' on-label ads stay with 'quiet the food noise'. Telehealth firms sell low-dose oral subscriptions as calm, focus and freedom from craving. The leader, Halcyon's 'Quiet' plan ($149 pill + $30 clinician fee), has about 400k subscribers, roughly 5% of the ~8.4M cash payers. The label and the marketing describe the same effect at different doses.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Tech, trading and consulting have an open low-dose culture, with workers citing fewer distractions, less snacking and less late-night drinking. Managers report steadier but less ambitious performers, and no study separates the two. No employer requires or pays for it as a productivity aid.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians and comedians talk publicly about coming off to 'get the hunger back'. 'Unmedicated' has become a selling point in indie music press. Bars have lost the binge-weekend crowd, and the new social formats are sober daytime runs, feasts and climbing gyms. Users still report dulled enjoyment, and sour, spicy and extreme flavours remain popular.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: With the effect named on the label, partners negotiate dose reductions around holidays and anniversaries. Couples therapists report 'dose conflicts' as a presenting issue. There is no quantified effect on relationship outcomes.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No measurable turnout or polarisation effect. Rhetorically, 'unmedicated' has become a crossover identity used by both wellness-left and MAHA-right commentators against 'sedated America'. Political reporters note it as a theme in 2028 campaign messaging, not a policy.

state.regulatory_posture: Still pro-access and pro-speed. Priority vouchers were used for retatrutide, and oral semaglutide 50 mg was reviewed quickly. The anhedonia class labelling followed routine pharmacovigilance. There has been no new state initiative this step. FDA has not acted against 'calm/focus' telehealth marketing, which stays within labelled 'food noise' language plus off-label prescribing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Medicare Bridge was extended on unchanged terms ($245 / $50 copay). Medicaid covers obesity at the same rate in 14 states. TrumpRx and direct channels carry the price steps.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged: BMI/comorbidity thresholds and prior authorisation. No adherence monitoring or benefit conditioning.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The gap between US cash prices ($149–299) and generics in India ($8–48) and Canada (CAD 70–110) is still a talking point. Small-scale personal importation is tolerated, and US exclusivity runs to about 2031–32. Manufacturers continue to trade price steps for tariff relief and Medicare access.

events.event: The American Society of Addiction Medicine issues a conditional recommendation for semaglutide in alcohol use disorder with comorbid obesity or type 2 diabetes. The VA adds it to formulary for AUD, and Novo files a supplemental FDA application in June 2028.

FDA requires a class labelling change adding 'anhedonia/emotional blunting' to incretin labels. It cites a postmarketing study finding clinically meaningful reward blunting in about 4% of patients vs 1.5% on placebo, reversible with dose reduction in most.
FDA approves a 50 mg dose of the Wegovy pill after a head-to-head trial shows the daily oral is non-inferior to the weekly Wegovy injection, at about 16% weight loss. Novo prices it at $199 cash.

New TrumpRx and manufacturer cash prices take effect: injectables $199–299, pills from $149. CMS extends the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2029 on the same $245/$50 terms, and employer coverage for weight loss slips to 56%.
Telehealth firm Halcyon reports 400,000 subscribers to its $179/month 'Quiet' plan, a low-dose oral GLP-1 marketed for calm, focus and 'freedom from craving'. The plan's ads never mention weight.
'#unmedicated' passes 2 billion TikTok views. Brooklyn and LA 'feast' supper clubs and strength gyms market to it, and an Equinox 'Unmedicated Strength' class line sells out in New York.

open_tensions: The label says emotional blunting is an adverse effect in 4% of patients, while a cash market of hundreds of thousands pays for subclinical blunting as 'calm'. No regulator has decided whether selling the side effect is promotion.

Adoption has plateaued near 11–12% while prices fall. A third of ever-users are cycling, employers keep retreating, and the 2031–32 generic cliff will reset who pays before anyone knows what a decade of cycling does.
Semaglutide is becoming addiction medicine just as the culture recasts appetite as vitality. Heavy drinkers are told to take it while affluent young adults signal status by refusing it.
Medicare's Bridge is a demonstration extended on unchanged terms, not a law. Rising over-65 use is meeting an accumulating lean-mass and bone signal in exactly that group.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US; brand exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
Medicare pays about $245/month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay for obesity GLP-1s under the GLP-1 Bridge terms.
Indian generic semaglutide still sells at roughly $8–48/month.
The suicidal-ideation warning remains removed from the Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound labels.
Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly remain the duopoly holding nearly all US incretin sales; Starbucks has not restored weight-loss coverage.

prose.headline: Thin Is Cheap Now: the $149 pill, the 4% warning label, and the young rich who brag about being hungry
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 a little under one American adult in eight takes an incretin drug, almost exactly as many as two years ago. The flat number hides a lot of movement. Nearly a fifth of adults have now tried one. About a third of those have quit and come back at least once, and some have done it more than once. People come in because the price keeps stepping down. A daily pill now works as well as the weekly Wegovy shot, and it starts at $149 a month in cash. People leave because their employer stopped paying, because the nausea never settled, or because they were simply done. The country is not adopting the drug so much as living alongside it.

Who pays has not changed. Medicare still pays $245 a month and its beneficiaries $50, under a demonstration that was extended rather than written into law. Over-65 use has crept up because of it. Fourteen state Medicaid programmes pay the same rate. A little over half of large employers still cover weight loss, and the share falls slightly every renewal season. Everyone else pays cash through TrumpRx or the manufacturers' own stores, at $199 to $299 for injectables. Lilly's new triple agonist, retatrutide, brings the best result to about 28% of body weight. In India the same semaglutide molecule sells for the price of a cinema ticket. US exclusivity runs to the early 2030s, and nobody in Washington is in a hurry to change that.

Two things about the drug's effect on the mind became official. In mid-2027 addiction doctors formally endorsed semaglutide for alcohol use disorder in patients who also have obesity or diabetes. Addiction clinics now prescribe it to heavy drinkers without obesity too, off-label. The spirits industry, which depends on its heaviest customers, has watched late-night volume thin out. Three months later the FDA added emotional blunting to the label, with a number: about 4% of patients on maintenance doses, against 1.5% on placebo, mostly reversible with a lower dose. It is one mechanism, recorded on the same label once as a treatment and once as a risk.

The market found the gap. Telehealth firms sell low-dose pills to the people who qualify on the label and want something else: calm, focus, a quieter head at 11pm. Halcyon's 'Quiet' plan never mentions weight. It has four hundred thousand subscribers, many of them in finance and software. The FDA has said nothing, and no new rule obliges it to.

Culture has moved as the price fell, though not everywhere. Among college-educated twenty- and thirty-somethings in Brooklyn, Silver Lake and East Austin, a merely thin body now reads as a prescription. What signals status is the expensive part: visible muscle, a trainer, finishing the plate. 'Unmedicated' has become a hashtag, a dating-app tag, a gym class and an insult. Feast-style supper clubs sell out, while plus-size retailers keep closing stores two miles away. In Dayton and Tulsa, losing forty pounds is still just good news. The bottom income third uses the drug least of all, and for many of those families it is still what they are trying to reach.

The economy has adapted rather than broken. Snack makers sell protein and smaller packs, restaurants sell smaller plates at higher prices, and gyms sell strength. Insurers are not paying out more, and pharmacy cost growth has eased with net prices. Children are still a small story: about one adolescent with obesity in twenty-five is on the drug, mostly in households that can pay. Their long-term outcomes are still a blank in every dataset.

Nothing has collapsed. A drug now sold for calm carries a warning about calm that goes too far, and both are true at once.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marcus Bell opens the Brass Rail on North Water Street in Milwaukee at three. He counts the till float twice because he likes to. The Thursday whiskey flight has been cut down to two pours, and the distributor rep doesn't bother pushing the new bourbon any more.

At lunch he takes the pill, 50 milligrams, with the required four ounces of water and thirty minutes before coffee. It costs $199 on his card, because the restaurant group's plan stopped covering weight loss in January. His doctor wrote 'alcohol use disorder, obesity' on the chart and didn't make a speech about it.

He has the insert folded in his wallet. He never meant to keep it. Section 6, emotional blunting, four percent.

His regulars are thinner than they were and stay a shorter time. Gary orders a soda water with bitters and tips like he used to drink. Two kids in Carhartt order the smash burger with double fries and eat every bite, loudly, the way people did before.

Around seven his daughter Keisha texts a photo from her climbing gym in Bay View. Her forearms are chalked. Under it she writes: 'unmedicated and starving lol, pizza Sunday?'

He types 'yes' and stares at it. He likes pizza. He thinks he still likes pizza. He tries to remember the last time he wanted something badly, and he can't tell if that's the drug or being fifty-four.

At close he wipes down the taps and pours himself nothing. He drives home with the radio off and doesn't notice it's off until he's in the driveway.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Retatrutide's BLA was filed in Mar 2027 and approved in Apr 2028 under a priority voucher.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: a priority voucher implies a review of weeks to a couple of months (Foundayo took 50 days), yet this approval took 13 months. The voucher looks bolted on to justify the approval, and the timeline contradicts its own stated mechanism.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The FDA-required Foundayo postmarketing study used the validated SHAPS anhedonia scale.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: Foundayo was approved Apr 2026, and a postmarketing study pooled with Sentinel data is said to have reported and driven a class-wide label change by Sep 2027. That is about 17 months for a new endpoint, and the start-to-label chain is asserted rather than shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: FDA sNDA for semaglutide filed Jun 2028, under review
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the parent has only one n=108 RCT and a phase 2 oral study for AUD, and the candidate shows no phase 3 trial or readout. A filing within two years, preceded by an ASAM guideline and VA formulary listing, skips the evidence chain.

rationale.badness: This is a modestly harder society with new losers. About 0.75M excess adults have drug-attributable reward blunting. A third of ever-users cycle with no outcome data, and the bottom income third uses the drug least (7.5%) while the thin body becomes a class marker. Public health is mixed: the 503B exclusion cut compounded harms, and the AUD indication is a real benefit. Epistemic badness is low because the blunting is labelled, measured and discussable, though the regulatory gap over selling it as 'calm' is noted. Cohesion costs ('dose conflicts' in couples, 'unmedicated' as an insult) are real but contained.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised. Adoption is +0.5pp, prices decline in managed steps, coverage is unchanged, AUD and the anhedonia label are in the events, oral parity comes as the allowed 50 mg new form, Halcyon sells the marketed feature, and the culture inverts. The one wrinkle is the Bridge extension and 503B finalisation, which sit loosely against state_action none; both are status quo or already in motion. mechanism: the world loses points for the three claims listed above (voucher versus 13-month review, a fast anhedonia study and class label, an AUD filing without phase 3 evidence), and for the ASAM guideline resting on thin evidence. Some causal chains are well shown, such as flat adoption from churn, orals and the employer retreat, but many attributions are asserted. magnitude: on-drug 11.5 and ever-used 18 sit inside the envelope, and the income and age splits bracket and average correctly. The approvals obey the timing rules: CagriSema was under review, retatrutide came 13 months after filing, survodutide is still pending, and amycretin is unfiled. The payer mix sums to 30M, Medicare $4.7B matches the CBO pace, Halcyon is about 5% of cash payers, and the cycling arithmetic closes. The only blemishes are the ambiguous 6.8M Medicare figure used both as newly eligible and as total users, and ever-used sitting near the top of its band.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The VA adds it to formulary for AUD, and Novo files a supplemental FDA application in June 2028.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the event is dated 2027-06 but contains a June 2028 filing. Novo also files an AUD sNDA with no phase 3 programme shown, only the n=108 Lancet RCT and a phase 2 oral study from the parent world.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The FDA-required Foundayo postmarketing study used the validated SHAPS anhedonia scale. Pooled with Sentinel claims data, it found clinically meaningful reward blunting in about 4% of patients on maintenance doses vs about 1.5% on placebo.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: Foundayo was approved Apr 2026, and a placebo-controlled postmarketing study is reported and turned into a class label by Sep 2027, which is very fast. Claims data cannot measure SHAPS scores, so 'pooling' them is incoherent.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Novo's oral semaglutide 50 mg was filed as an sNDA in Jan 2027 and approved in Oct 2027 after a 68-week head-to-head trial.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: a 68-week head-to-head trial finished before a Jan 2027 filing must have started by about Aug 2025. That is before oral Wegovy was approved, and the parent world mentions no such trial. The parity timeline is asserted rather than derived.

rationale.badness: This is a modestly harder version of 2026. About 4% clinically meaningful blunting is now labelled, and 'dose conflicts' show up in couples therapy. Thinness is cheap while the bottom income third sits at 7.5% use, children's use skews affluent, and employer coverage keeps eroding. Harm is named and measured (label, SHAPS), which keeps epistemic and public-health scores low. The marketing of subclinical blunting as 'calm' (Halcyon, 400k subscribers) and the rebound-drinking case series add real but bounded harm. Nothing is melodramatic.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised. Adoption is +0.5pp, prices follow managed decline, and the anhedonia label, oral parity (existing product in a new form), AUD indication (guideline plus filing), aesthetic inversion and marketed-feature layer all appear in fields and events. The Bridge extension and the 503B finalisation sit slightly awkwardly against state_action none and coverage status_quo, but they are continuations. mechanism: Most chains are shown (price steps, employer retreat, ASAM to AUD prescribing, label to telehealth framing). The weak links are the three listed claims: the AUD sNDA with no pivotal trial and a mis-dated event, the implausibly fast SHAPS postmarketing study pooled with claims data, and the 68-week trial timeline. The 2 billion TikTok views and the 'exposed influencers' line are also merely asserted. magnitude: On-drug 11.5, ever-used 18 (near the 18.5 edge) and the income and age bands are inside the envelope and average correctly. The payer mix sums to 30M. Medicare and Medicaid spend ($4.7B, $2.6B) multiplies out, retatrutide approval comes 13 months after filing, and no US generic appears. Small gaps remain: the pediatric 0.4% of under-18s against 4% of adolescents with obesity, the 65+ rise of 1.5pp against 1.6M Bridge users, and Medicare 'users' coincidentally equal to the newly eligible 6.8M.
rationale.generativity: The world has strong implied scenes: 'feast' supper clubs, the Equinox 'Unmedicated Strength' class, Halcyon's 'Quiet' plan, dose negotiations around anniversaries, and the label folded in a wallet. The Marcus Bell bar scene shows rather than explains. The unnoticed radio, the 'pizza Sunday?' text and the 'drug or being fifty-four' line carry the theme through texture, and the minor characters (Gary, Keisha) feel real.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pooled with Sentinel claims data, it found clinically meaningful reward blunting in about 4% of patients on maintenance doses vs about 1.5% on placebo.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a postmarketing study of a drug approved in Apr 2026 is said to have enrolled, measured with SHAPS, pooled with claims data and driven a class-wide label by Sep 2027. That is very fast, and a single-drug study is asserted to generalise to every incretin. The 1.5% placebo arm and the doubling of risk with prior depression are stated with no shown chain.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Novo's oral semaglutide 50 mg was filed as an sNDA in Jan 2027 and approved in Oct 2027 after a 68-week head-to-head trial.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: a 68-week head-to-head trial must have started by about mid-2025 and read out by late 2026, yet the parent world mentions no such trial. The approval timing is allowed by the envelope, but the trial history is asserted, not derived from the parent.

least_plausible_claims.quote: This is concentrated at ages 12–17, where roughly 4% of adolescents with obesity are on a drug.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the parent had only about 0.6% of children with obesity on a drug, and overall adult adoption is flat here. A roughly sixfold jump in adolescent use in two years has no mechanism, and the 0.4% of all under-18s figure is barely reconciled with it.

rationale.badness: This is a recognisably harder but adapted society. About 4% of users have labelled blunting, and 'dose conflicts' show up in couples therapy. The bottom income third uses the drug least (7.5%) while the affluent young perform 'unmedicated' as status, and adolescent use skews to households that can pay. The anhedonia harm is measured, labelled and discussable, which keeps the epistemic score low, and nothing here is catastrophic.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised and tied to a dated event or field: AUD indication, anhedonia label, oral parity via the 50 mg sNDA, managed price decline, aesthetic inversion, marketed-feature personality layer and the +0.5pp adoption move. The VA formulary addition and the CMS Bridge extension sit slightly awkwardly against `state_action: none`, and the Foundayo-based class label is thinly tied to its driver. mechanism: most chains are shown, such as employer retreat lowering 50–64 use and the Medicare Bridge raising 65+ use. Several are asserted, namely the fast SHAPS postmarketing study behind a class-wide label (claim 1), the 68-week oral trial with no parent basis (claim 2) and the unexplained adolescent uptake (claim 3). Spirits volume down 3–4% and orals at 60% of new starts are also asserted. magnitude: every population figure is inside the envelope (11.5, 18, income thirds averaging 11.5, age weights summing to 11.5), and the approvals respect the rules (retatrutide filed Mar 2027, approved Apr 2028; no US generic). The reconciliations hold: 1.6M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.7B, Medicare's 6.8M eligible is about 10% of enrollees, payer mix sums to 30M, Halcyon is about 5% of cash payers, and the 30% cycling arithmetic works. Minor gaps remain: 6.8M is reused for both Medicare users and the newly eligible, the adolescent share (claim 3) is aggressive, and the cash-price high of $299 ignores the surviving list price.
rationale.generativity: The world is rich in implied scenes: Brooklyn feast supper clubs, the Equinox 'Unmedicated Strength' class, Halcyon's 'Quiet' subscribers, dose negotiations around anniversaries, and exposed 'unmedicated' influencers on low doses. The Marcus Bell vignette shows rather than explains: the folded insert, the radio he doesn't notice is off, and the 'drug or being fifty-four' ambiguity. Keisha's text adds a second character who anchors the cultural inversion. The prose is good, though the opening is mostly summary.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Retatrutide's BLA was filed in Mar 2027 and approved in Apr 2028 under a priority voucher.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: a priority voucher implies a review of weeks to a couple of months (Foundayo took 50 days), yet this approval took 13 months. The voucher looks bolted on to justify the approval, and the timeline contradicts its own stated mechanism.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The FDA-required Foundayo postmarketing study used the validated SHAPS anhedonia scale.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: Foundayo was approved Apr 2026, and a postmarketing study pooled with Sentinel data is said to have reported and driven a class-wide label change by Sep 2027. That is about 17 months for a new endpoint, and the start-to-label chain is asserted rather than shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: FDA sNDA for semaglutide filed Jun 2028, under review
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the parent has only one n=108 RCT and a phase 2 oral study for AUD, and the candidate shows no phase 3 trial or readout. A filing within two years, preceded by an ASAM guideline and VA formulary listing, skips the evidence chain.

rationale.badness: This is a modestly harder society with new losers. About 0.75M excess adults have drug-attributable reward blunting. A third of ever-users cycle with no outcome data, and the bottom income third uses the drug least (7.5%) while the thin body becomes a class marker. Public health is mixed: the 503B exclusion cut compounded harms, and the AUD indication is a real benefit. Epistemic badness is low because the blunting is labelled, measured and discussable, though the regulatory gap over selling it as 'calm' is noted. Cohesion costs ('dose conflicts' in couples, 'unmedicated' as an insult) are real but contained.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised. Adoption is +0.5pp, prices decline in managed steps, coverage is unchanged, AUD and the anhedonia label are in the events, oral parity comes as the allowed 50 mg new form, Halcyon sells the marketed feature, and the culture inverts. The one wrinkle is the Bridge extension and 503B finalisation, which sit loosely against state_action none; both are status quo or already in motion. mechanism: the world loses points for the three claims listed above (voucher versus 13-month review, a fast anhedonia study and class label, an AUD filing without phase 3 evidence), and for the ASAM guideline resting on thin evidence. Some causal chains are well shown, such as flat adoption from churn, orals and the employer retreat, but many attributions are asserted. magnitude: on-drug 11.5 and ever-used 18 sit inside the envelope, and the income and age splits bracket and average correctly. The approvals obey the timing rules: CagriSema was under review, retatrutide came 13 months after filing, survodutide is still pending, and amycretin is unfiled. The payer mix sums to 30M, Medicare $4.7B matches the CBO pace, Halcyon is about 5% of cash payers, and the cycling arithmetic closes. The only blemishes are the ambiguous 6.8M Medicare figure used both as newly eligible and as total users, and ever-used sitting near the top of its band.
